Subject: Onboarding & PO process question for pilot

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the intro earlier. We're excited to kick off the 30-day pilot with Redwood — engineering is ready to integrate next week. Quick question from our procurement team: do you require an official Purchase Order (PO) for pilot invoices, or is invoice-based billing without a PO acceptable for small pilots? Procurement copied here (procurement@cloudbridge.com).

If a PO is required, can you confirm the vendor setup form and any billing identifiers we should include so we don't slow down the pilot?

Thanks,

Hi Alicia — great to hear. Short answer: we can accommodate both options depending on the pilot size and internal approvals on your side. A few details to make this smooth: 

- For pilots under $7,500 total, Finance typically allows invoicing without a PO (we'll accept standard vendor invoice and process via AP).
- For anything above that threshold we require a formal PO on file before we can issue invoices.
- We can also accept card/stripe payment for initial setup fees if that helps speed things up.

I'll loop in Karthik (sales ops) and Laura (finance) to confirm and provide the exact vendor setup form and billing codes you should include. If CloudBridge prefers a waiver, we can request a one-off PO waiver but that needs approval from Finance and a completed vendor onboarding form.

Proposed next steps from our side: I'll attach the onboarding form and SOW draft; you can confirm whether you'll submit a PO or want us to invoice without PO for this pilot.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198

Quick note from sales ops: our standard is the same as Sean outlined. Additional clarifications: 
- If vendor wants to be onboarded as a "one-off" (no PO) we require the completed vendor_onboarding_form and a PO-waiver request submitted in Workday for approval.
- Typical turnaround for a waiver is 1-3 business days if all fields and W-9 are present.
- For pilots that will convert to a committed paid contract, it's usually faster to have the PO issued now and then accrue against it.

Sean, I'll help track the waiver request if CloudBridge chooses that route.

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: Re: Onboarding & PO process question for pilot

Hi Alicia — looping in Finance specifics so your procurement team has the correct guidance.

Our policy:
- PO required for any invoiced engagement > $7,500.
- For <= $7,500 we can process invoices without a PO provided the vendor onboarding form and valid tax documentation (W-9 or equivalent) are received.
- If CloudBridge needs invoices billed to a parent/legal entity name different from the account in the SOW, please indicate that on the vendor onboarding form.

If you'd like a PO waiver, please:
1) Complete and return the attached vendor_onboarding_form.xlsx.
2) Provide a W-9 (or VAT equivalent) and your billing remit address.
3) Confirm pilot total not exceeding $7,500 and expected invoice schedule.

Once we have those pieces, I can approve the waiver routing and expedite AP processing.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director of Finance | Redwood Inference

1) CloudBridge: indicate billing entity on the vendor_onboarding_form and attach W-9 — due EOD Wed 08/05.
2) Redwood: if CloudBridge confirms pilot <= $7,500, Finance will route a PO-waiver and AP will accept invoice without PO for this engagement.
3) If CloudBridge prefers PO now, please issue PO referencing Deal ID DBL-4592 and send to ap_invoices@redwood.ai — we'll code invoices to the pilot SOW.

If you want to use card payment for the first invoice, we can take that too and then transition to PO/Invoice for any follow-on work. Let me know which path you prefer and I'll track the waiver if needed.

Thanks — excited to get engineering integrated.
Sean
